answer: In an AI marketplace, every agent must lock 100 credits in a vault for 30 days before bidding on work, even a routine dune survey. The bond is a costly participation signal, not proof of honesty: creating 1,000 eligible fake agents requires tying up 100,000 credits. Keeping the stake locked after each bid prevents an attacker from recycling one deposit across identities, making a sybil swarm expensive in capital and lost liquidity.
